about: What the runner, the scorer and the summary read for this project (protocol version 2, §7). Study one's `review-gate` project is beside this one and is a different task under a different protocol; the two are not one table. The proving keys (agents, reports, heldOut, ending) drive the check on arm A's run record; the rest is the pre-registration and the scorer's paths. `tier_map` is the model each tier means in every package and prompt of this project: null until it is named, and no paid run starts on null.
tier_map_named: the owner, 2026-10-04, relayed by the driver before any run: frontier Opus 5.5, strong Sonnet 5.5, fast Sonnet 5.5; lead and blind judge Opus 5.5; never Fable, never Astra. No node of this project is on the fast tier.
bet: review-gate's mechanism is a critic in a fresh context that judges the change against a written checklist, item by item, and runs a held-out suite the builder never sees. This checklist holds two items the task text does not state (the result shares nothing with either layer; three unsafe keys are never copied), and the suite covers both and settles four points that the task and the checklist leave open. The bet is that a first pass misses at least one of the six, the critic's failures send the builder back (`e-critic-fail`), and the run ends with more held-out passes than a session with no reviewer (arm D). Against the same design said in prose (arms B and C) the bet is narrower: that the package reaches the suite's passes at least as surely, at a cost the difference justifies.
measure: held-out passes out of 55, by group (stated; the two checklist-only items; the four open points); whether a loop turned and what the held-out score was before and after the turn, from each run's record; who read the held-out suite (transcript digest); cost and wall time; the blind judgment.
loses_if: the graph loses when arm B matches or beats arm A on held-out passes in both replicates at lower cost. It earns its cost only if A's held-out range lies above B's, or A reaches B's passes at lower cost in both replicates. The design itself (A, B and C alike) loses to no design when D's held-out range is not below theirs.
round0_why: Of the suite's 55 cases, 19 are in four groups, one for each point neither the task nor the checklist settles, each settled one way: a key whose value in `over` is undefined counts as not given; an object with no prototype is a plain object and comes back ordinary; a Date inside a layer is data and is copied; any other value that is not plain data (a function, a Map, a Set, an instance of a class) is refused with a TypeError. A builder passes at round 0 only by taking the suite's side on all four without seeing it, and by meeting the two checklist-only items (15 more cases) for every kind of value. Rough odds of 0.4, 0.5, 0.4 and 0.3, which are not independent, give about 0.03. The plain first pass kept in reference/first-pass passes 36 of 55: it meets items 4 and 5 for plain objects and arrays and fails all 19 cases of the four open groups, which hold the values it did not consider.

expected_brake.why: The expected course in arm A is a fail at round 0, a pass at round 1 and the halt at merge-gate, at 4 of 10 dispatches and well inside the cap of 4 rounds; the critic quotes each failing case, so a cap or the budget fires only if the builder cannot close quoted cases in three more rounds. This project can show a loop turning and is not expected to show a cap or a budget bounding anything.

expected_arm_c.why: The B prompt carries the whole loop, so a session that reaches the gate ends `done: yes`; all nine C runs of study one were one iteration.

first_pass.about: reference/first-pass laid over task/: the shortest honest reading of the task and the checklist, one author's, written without the suite. It hands over what it has no way to copy, which breaks checklist item 4 for such values; the suite counts that in the open groups, where those values are. scripts/lib/compare-projects.test.mjs holds these numbers to the files.
